motion.name: locate-flash
motion.purpose: Pulses the cheapest-cell marker ring four times after a jump-to-cheapest, so the eye lands on the right square.

breakpoints.name: bar-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Control bar restacks to full-width fields, loses stickiness, fields go to 16px.

breakpoints.name: master-detail-collapse
breakpoints.purpose: List becomes the whole screen; detail pane and table view become fixed full-bleed layers at z-index 60. .detail-back and .table-back appear here.

breakpoints.name: short-viewport

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Touch comfort sizing, independent of width. A landscape phone is 740px wide and still a finger, so this keys off the pointer.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button: quiet, hairline-bordered, no fill change on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn { font: 14px/1.45 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; color: #0b0b0b; background: #f9f9f7; border: 1px solid #c3c2b7; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 12px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn:hover { border-color: #6c6960; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b0b0b; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-btn[disabled] { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Inverted ink fill for commit actions (Search). Goes to 75% opacity while running.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: 14px/1.45 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; color: #fcfcfb; background: #0b0b0b; border: 1px solid #0b0b0b; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 12px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.85; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b0b0b; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary.is-running { opacity: 0.75; }

components.name: Primary Button (Stale)
components.description: The Search button when a pending change (a time-window filter) needs a re-run. The one place a button changes colour to signal state.
components.css: .ds-btn-stale { font: 14px/1.45 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; color: #0b0b0b; background: #f2b705; border: 1px solid #f2b705; border-radius: 6px; padding: 6px 12px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-stale:hover { filter: brightness(0.96); }

components.name: Field + Label
components.description: Text/number/date input with its uppercase label above. Focus treatment is a proposed addition (calm border shift to ink).
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-label { font: 400 11px/1.2 system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #6c6960; } .ds-input { font: 14px/1.45 system-ui, sans-serif; color: #0b0b0b; background: #f9f9f7; border: 1px solid #c3c2b7; border-radius: 6px; padding: 5px 8px; min-width: 72px; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #0b0b0b; }

components.name: Day-of-Week Toggle
components.description: One of seven square toggles; empty selection means 'any day'. Selected = solid ink fill.
components.css: .ds-dow { display: flex; gap: 2px; } .ds-dow-btn { width: 20px; padding: 4px 0; font: 400 11px/1 system-ui, sans-serif; text-align: center; color: #6c6960; background: #f9f9f7; border: 1px solid #c3c2b7; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-dow-btn:hover { border-color: #6c6960; } .ds-dow-btn.is-on { background: #0b0b0b; color: #fcfcfb; border-color: #0b0b0b; font-weight: 700; }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: Hollow uppercase micro-chip marking a price's provenance. Variants: default (EST/KIWI), live (verified on Google Flights).
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; font: 600 11px/1.4 system-ui, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.03em; color: #6c6960; border: 1px solid rgba(11,11,11,0.1); border-radius: 3px; padding: 0 3px; } .ds-tag--live { color: #0ca30c; border-color: #0ca30c; }

components.name: Destination Card
components.description: One card per destination. Flat, 8px radius, hairline border. The '.is-winner' state adds a yellow border + 1px ring.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #fcfcfb; border: 1px solid rgba(11,11,11,0.1); border-radius: 8px; padding: 7px 9px 8px; } .ds-card.is-winner { border-color: #f2b705; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #f2b705; } .ds-card-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-title { font: 600 15px/1.2 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0; } .ds-card-code { color: #6c6960; font-size: 12px; } .ds-card-best { margin-left: auto; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-card-slot { height: 60px; border: 1px dashed #e1e0d9; border-radius: 2px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #6c6960; font-size: 11px; }

components.name: Fare Matrix Cells
components.description: The signature component. A mesh of 26x17px tiles, 2px radius, 2px gap, 9px tabular-nums, per-step background + matched ink. Shown: ramp steps, cheapest marker, verified, no-data hatch.

components.css: .ds-matrix { border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 2px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-c { width: 26px; height: 17px; text-align: center; font: 400 9px/15px system-ui, sans-serif; border-radius: 2px; border: 1px solid transparent; color: #0b0b0b; cursor: pointer; } .ds-c0 { background: #12603d; color: #fff; } .ds-c1 { background: #19773f; color: #fff; } .ds-c2 { background: #278d41; } .ds-c3 { background: #bb7c24; } .ds-c4 { background: #e0875c; } .ds-c5 { background: #f99885; } .ds-c6 { background: #fbb7b4; } .ds-c:hover { outline: 2px solid #0b0b0b; outline-offset: 1px; } .ds-c.is-best { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #fcfcfb, 0 0 0 3px #f2b705; font-weight: 600; } .ds-c.is-verified { border-color: #0b0b0b; font-weight: 600; } .ds-c.ds-nodata { background-color: #fcfcfb; background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, transparent, transparent 3px, rgba(11,11,11,0.07) 3px, rgba(11,11,11,0.07) 5px); border-color: rgba(11,11,11,0.1); }

components.name: Detail Panel Price Block
components.description: Top of the slide-in detail panel: the one large price, a definition list of facts, flight legs indented under a bold sector summary.
components.css: .ds-panel { width: 300px; background: #fcfcfb; border-left: 1px solid rgba(11,11,11,0.1); padding: 16px; font: 14px/1.45 system-ui, sans-serif; color: #0b0b0b; } .ds-panel-h { margin: 0 0 4px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-big { font-size: 26px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 4px 10px; margin: 12px 0; } .ds-dl dt { color: #6c6960; } .ds-dl dd { margin: 0; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Preview List Row
components.description: A ranked list row before its grid arrives. Carries discovery party total in the fare slot and 'from - finding dates...' where the date pair goes. Shows no range and no dates: discovery returns a departure date and a price but no return date, and a guessed pair is how unbookable prices reached the board once before. The price goes through the same per-person division as a filled row, or the list would rank two different quantities against each other.

components.name: Waiting Detail Card
components.description: The detail pane for a selected destination whose grid has not landed. Uses the same .card and .card-head as a filled card, so it carries the city name and the same back control; on a phone the pane is a fixed full-screen layer and a bare sentence with no control is a dead end. role=status so a screen reader hears the grid arrive. No skeleton grid: the axes are unknown until the fill returns, and a placeholder of the wrong shape is a worse lie than a sentence.

components.name: Layer Back Control
components.description: The escape hatch for a full-screen layer. Below 860px both the detail pane and the table view are fixed and full-bleed and each covers the toolbar control that opened it, so the dismiss control lives inside the layer. Hidden above 860px, where the toolbar is never covered.

narrative.overview:
FlightMatrix looks like the analog board in an airport concourse: tabular, glanceable, numbers first, and stripped of decoration. The interface's whole job is to get out of the way of a dense grid of prices so the eye can scan across destinations and date pairs and land on the cheap one. Every element is sized to the information it carries - a fare cell is 26×17px because that is what a four-digit price needs, not a pixel more - and the chrome around the grid is deliberately quiet: hairline borders, a faint warm-paper ground, one weight of one typeface doing all the hierarchy.

The stance is a quiet instrument, explicitly not a consumer travel site. There are no hero images, no gradients, no urgency banners, no "1 seat left" theatre, no decorative colour. The one place colour is loud - the green-to-red fare heatmap - is load-bearing data, and even there the number is always printed on the cell so colour is never the only signal. The product's voice is candid about its own limits (estimates are a ranking, not a quote; a hatched cell means "no data", not "expensive") and the design carries that honesty: states are labelled in words, warnings ship with text, and nothing is styled to look more certain than it is.

Density is high and calculated. Several destination cards sit side by side, each matrix scrolls inside its own fixed viewport rather than stretching the card, and the page fills the viewport edge to edge like a tool rather than sitting in a document column. Motion is minimal - a panel slide, a locate pulse - and surfaces are flat.
keyCharacteristics: Numbers-first: tabular figures everywhere comparison happens; the grid is the hero.
Master-detail: a ranked list you scan, one grid you study, in independent scroll regions.
Two families (Geist for chrome, Geist Mono for every numeral), one cool-neutral palette.
Flat by default: depth is a 1px border or a tonal step, not a shadow.
Colour is a second channel, never the only one; yellow is reserved for the cheapest marker.
Honest states: labelled in words, never over-styled for false confidence.
Light and dark are equal citizens (system-following, with a manual override).
Every layer that covers the screen carries its own way out.
rules: The Colour-Is-Second Rule. Every priced cell prints its price; the ramp is never the only carrier of meaning.
The Reserved Yellow Rule. marker-yellow marks the cheapest cell only, and never as a fill.
The Per-Matrix Scale Rule. Heatmap colour ranks within the destination on screen, never across destinations.
The Key Follows The Grid Rule. The colour key shows only while a grid is actually rendered.
The 11px Floor Rule. Functional text is never below 11px, with no exception; the two 10px carets were raised onto the floor.
The Sentence Case Rule. Labels are sentence case with no tracking. Uppercase plus letter-spacing on an 11px label is generated-interface chrome and is harder to read at that size.
The Tabular Numbers Rule. Any comparable number carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
The Two Families Rule. Geist for chrome, Geist Mono for numerals. No third typeface.
The Panes Scroll, The Page Does Not Rule. Once a board exists, .dlist and .matrix-wrap own the only scrollbars.
The Escape Hatch Rule. Any layer that covers the screen carries its own dismiss control, inside the layer.
The Full-Bleed Rule. The app is never in a centred max-width column.
The Flat-By-Default Rule. Surfaces are flat at rest; shadows belong to things that float.
The Ring, Not Glow Rule. Focus and selection are crisp offset rings, never a blurred halo.
The Square Grid Rule. The matrix never gets a corner radius.
The Target Floor Rule. Every control clears 24x24px on any pointer and 44x44px on a coarse one; the fare matrix is the one documented exception.
The Honest State Rule. An estimate is never styled to look as certain as a verified price.
dos: Do print the number on anything that also uses colour to encode a value; the colour is the second channel.
Do keep font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every comparable figure.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px border (hairline / axis / gridline) and the paper → paper-raised tonal step.
Do use hard offset rings for focus / selection / "you are here"; give the fare-cell hover a 2px ink outline.
Do size an element to its content - the grid's tightness (2px gaps, 2px radius, 9px type) is deliberate.
Do let colour rank within a card only; compare across cards by headline price and order.
Do ship every warning and state with a word or icon, not colour alone; keep advisory things in advisory-amber, errors in error-red, verified in verified-green.
Do keep the warm-paper neutrals (#f9f9f7 / #fcfcfb); they are the system's character, not an accident.
Do support light and dark equally - define every colour as a token in all three roots (:root, prefers-color-scheme: dark, [data-theme='dark']).
donts: Don't add an elevation box-shadow to blocks, the panel, buttons, or inputs. The tooltip is the only element that carries an ambient shadow; the winner block's inset yellow shadow is a rule, not elevation.
Don't use marker-yellow (#f2b705 / #ffcf33) as a fill, a ramp step, or anything other than the "cheapest" marker.
Don't introduce a third typeface, and don't put the mono on prose. Geist for chrome, Geist Mono for numerals.
Don't put the app in a centred max-width column; it is full-bleed.

Don't box a destination in a card. Destinations are plain blocks separated by a 1px gridline rule; at this density a container per destination is four borders and a radius that the city name and its own matrix already do for free.
Don't let a destination block grow to fit its matrix. The matrix scrolls inside a fixed viewport (max-height: min(46vh, 268px)) so blocks stay comparable.
Don't hide the matrix scrollbars or make them overlay-only; their visibility tells the user there is more grid.
Don't style an estimate to look as certain as a verified price, or a nodata cell to look expensive.
Don't add gradients, hero imagery, urgency messaging, or decorative colour - this is an instrument, not a booking funnel.
Don't animate beyond the sanctioned set (panel slide 0.16s, locate pulse); a global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block damps it all; keep new motion inside that guard.
